title: PLANT HEALTH: which individuals are actually working
question: New overlay on L (first press, ahead of CELL TYPE). Green = paying its upkeep, brightness is how well watered; red = failing to pay, brightness is how close to starving to death. Flat per plant, because it is one economic unit. Does this read at a glance -- and is the dark red of a just-started failure too dim to notice?
context_md: Lab bed, 24 founders, no colony, frame 9000, same seed both panes -- the overlay is render-only so the stand is identical. Counts at the frame shown: 126 plants, 6 paying their upkeep, 120 not -- but that headline is mostly seedlings, which have no leaf yet and cannot pay anything. Of the 11 ESTABLISHED plants (20+ cells), 8 are not paying and 3 are. None of the paying ones is short of water, so what limits this bed is carbon, not water. Note what the plain pane cannot tell you: each of those four clumps is a thriving plant standing next to a failing one, and they look identical without the overlay.

items.label: the bed as it draws now
